title: Relative Adjectives (Al-Nisbah) & Intensive Forms
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 40; Ryding Ch. 5 §5.7, Ch. 10)
objectives: Form nisbah adjectives (ـِيٌّ / ـِيَّةٌ) from nouns, removing tāʾ marbūṭah.
Recognize intensive adjectival patterns (ṣiyagh al-mubālaghah: فَعَّالٌ, فَعُولٌ, مِفْعَالٌ, فَعِيلٌ).
Parse intensive patterns frequent in divine attributes (al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 11: How do attributive adjectives agree with the noun they modify?

sections.heading: Al-Nisbah & Intensive Adjectives
sections.body: The relative adjective (al-nisbah) suffixes ـِيٌّ (fem. ـِيَّةٌ) to indicate origin, affiliation, or category (e.g., عَرَبٌ → عَرَبِيٌّ, مَكَّةُ → مَكِّيٌّ). Separately, intensive patterns (ṣiyagh al-mubālaghah) express habitual or superabundant performance of an action—central to classical divine attributes.

sections.label: Nisbah & Mubālaghah Rules
sections.summary: To form a nisbah: drop tāʾ marbūṭah (مَكَّةُ → مَكِّيٌّ) and suffix ـِيٌّ. Intensive patterns include فَعَّالٌ (غَفَّارٌ 'Ever-Forgiving'), فَعُولٌ (غَفُورٌ 'All-Forgiving', شَكُورٌ 'Most Appreciative'), and فَعِيلٌ (عَلِيمٌ 'All-Knowing', رَحِيمٌ).

sections.irab: اللَّهُ: لَفْظُ الجَلَالَةِ مُبْتَدَأٌ مَرْفُوعٌ | غَفُورٌ: خَبَرٌ أَوَّلُ (صِيغَةُ مُبَالَغَةٍ) | رَحِيمٌ: خَبَرٌ ثَانٍ مَرْفُوعٌ
sections.notes: Both غَفُورٌ (فَعُولٌ) and رَحِيمٌ (فَعِيلٌ) are intensive adjectival patterns.

sections.heading: Nisbah Sound Plurals
sections.body: Nisbah adjectives referring to human groups take sound masculine plurals (عَرَبِيُّونَ) or collective forms.
